findings.title: Resolving a live link deletes it
findings.description: The expiry comparison is reversed. A request for a live link removes it and gets a 404. An expired link can still resolve until the janitor removes it.

findings.title: A new owner's first create leaves a link behind and throws
findings.description: The link is inserted before indexing the quota dictionary. A new owner has no quota entry, so the lookup throws KeyNotFoundException. The caller receives no link code, but the store retains the link and subsequent creates for that owner fail the same way.

findings.title: A generated code collision silently replaces an existing link
findings.description: NewCode draws from a 31-bit range and Create assigns the result directly into the dictionary. A collision discards the existing link and its hit history, and the old short URL now points to the new target.

findings.title: The running service has no way to obtain a valid session
findings.description: Startup creates an empty Authenticator, and no startup code or HTTP route calls Issue or loads existing sessions. Every request with a well-formed bearer header receives a 401 before endpoint dispatch.

findings.title: A missing or one-part Authorization header aborts the request
findings.description: Handle passes an empty string when the header is absent. Splitting that value produces one element, so indexing the second element throws before the handler can send a 401 or close the response.

findings.title: A partial final page throws an out-of-range exception
findings.description: Page sets the end to one past the list count when fewer results remain than requested. GetRange then throws. For example, the default 20-item listing fails whenever the store contains 1 through 19 links.

findings.title: The stats handler divides by zero on an empty store
findings.description: The handler divides by store.Count before sending a response. It throws on a fresh store and whenever all links have been removed.

findings.title: Invalid numeric query values leave requests unanswered
findings.description: The TTL, offset, and size values are parsed with int.Parse outside error handling that can return a client response. Invalid text or an integer overflow faults the handler before it writes or closes the response.

findings.title: An unnamed report is written and then read from a different path
findings.description: With no name supplied, ExportCsv writes links.csv and returns its path. Report discards that path and attempts to read .csv, causing a 500 when that file is absent or serving unrelated contents when it exists.

findings.title: CSV exports corrupt fields containing commas, quotes, or line breaks
findings.description: ExportCsv and ArchiveAll interpolate raw fields into CSV. A comma in a destination URL, for example, shifts the owner and hit count into the wrong columns.

findings.title: Startup continues after configuration validation finds errors
findings.description: Validate returns true even after collecting problems, and Main discards the result. An out-of-range port reaches HttpListener startup, and an invalid cache size reaches the cache constructor.

findings.title: Cache TTL is interpreted in seconds instead of milliseconds
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is documented in milliseconds, but the value is passed to FromSeconds. A configured five-second lifetime becomes 5,000 seconds.

findings.title: Malformed numeric environment values overwrite defaults with zero
findings.description: A malformed LINKD_PORT sets Port to zero through the out parameter. A malformed LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS also sets Timeout to zero after logging that it is keeping the default.

findings.title: The fetch-limit override has no effect
findings.description: A valid positive LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is assigned back to the local variable. Config.Load always returns the default FetchLimit of 32.

findings.title: Configuration file read failures are silently ignored
findings.description: LoadFile treats every read exception as an empty file. A file that exists but is unreadable due to permissions or an I/O failure silently loses all of its overrides.

findings.title: Issued sessions never age out
findings.description: Verify returns matching sessions regardless of their ExpiresAt value. Each issued session also stays in memory indefinitely unless explicitly revoked, so the session table grows with issuance.

findings.title: A scheme prefix is accepted as a complete link target
findings.description: A value such as https:// passes the prefix check and can be stored even though it has no host and cannot serve as an absolute redirect destination.

findings.title: The create response interpolates unescaped JSON values
findings.description: Create accepts a destination containing quotes or backslashes and writes it directly inside a JSON string. The resulting response can contain invalid JSON or a destination different from the stored value.

findings.title: CSV and plain-text responses are labeled as JSON
findings.description: The response helper always sets application/json, including for the report CSV and the plain-text link listing. Clients that select a decoder from the content type attempt to parse these successful responses as JSON.

findings.title: Report generation fails when the export directory does not exist
findings.description: StreamWriter can create a report file but requires its parent directory to exist. The service never creates the configured export directory, so exporting to a fresh directory returns a 500.

findings.title: Reports silently omit links after the first 1,000
findings.description: The report endpoint always exports one page capped at 1,000 links and has no parameter for obtaining the rest. A report from a larger store looks complete while omitting every later link.

findings.title: Failed CSV writes leave file handles open
findings.description: ExportCsv and ArchiveAll call Close only after writing successfully. If a write throws, the handle stays open until garbage collection, so repeated failures can exhaust file descriptors.

findings.title: Snapshot replacement can overwrite the last good copy with a partial file
findings.description: The temporary file is under /tmp. If the destination is on another filesystem, File.Move can copy over the destination and delete the source. A crash during that copy can leave a partial snapshot. The write also lacks an explicit flush to disk before replacement.

findings.title: The asynchronous export drops every supplied link
findings.description: ExportCsvAsync ignores the links argument and overwrites the report with a header alone. A successful call can replace an existing report with an empty dataset.

findings.title: An asynchronous export write failure can terminate the process
findings.description: The method is async void, so a caller cannot await it or catch a write failure with a try block around the call. An exception from the file write can become an unhandled exception in the service process.

findings.title: A zero-sized cache crashes on insert and stats
findings.description: The configuration permits a capacity of zero. Set then selects a victim from an empty dictionary, and Utilization divides by zero.

findings.title: Cache eviction ignores recency and can evict on replacement
findings.description: The eviction code always selects the first dictionary key, even if that entry was just accessed. It also runs when overwriting an existing key, so a replacement can discard a different entry and leave the cache below capacity.

findings.title: Expired entries prevent warming until the next sweep
findings.description: Peek reports expired entries as present. Warm relies on that result and skips refreshing a stale entry, so the next Get returns a miss despite the warm call.

findings.title: Partial cache utilization is always reported as zero
findings.description: Integer division truncates the occupancy fraction before multiplication. A cache with 1,023 of 1,024 slots occupied reports 0 percent.

findings.title: The resolver never uses the configured cache
findings.description: Redirect reads directly from the store, and the running service only sweeps the cache and reads its utilization. Resolving links never populates or hits the cache, leaving the dashboard utilization at zero regardless of traffic.

findings.title: Lowercasing a code breaks links stored with uppercase letters
findings.description: Rename and ImportAll accept uppercase codes, and the store uses case-sensitive keys. Redirect lowercases the requested code, making an uppercase link unreachable or sending the request to a different lowercase link.

findings.title: Permanent outbound redirects can bypass click counting
findings.description: A client can cache the 301 response and send later clicks directly to the destination. Those clicks skip AddResolved, contrary to the endpoint's counting behavior.

findings.title: Local wall-clock changes alter link and cache lifetimes
findings.description: The store and cache compute and compare expiry times using DateTime.Now. A daylight-saving transition or clock adjustment can shorten or extend a configured TTL.

findings.title: Rename validates the source twice and accepts invalid destinations
findings.description: The second validation also checks from. Rename can remove a valid source and move it to an empty or otherwise invalid code.

findings.title: The follow percentage reports zero until every link has been followed
findings.description: The integer division discards the fraction before converting it to a percentage. One followed link out of two is reported as 0 percent.

findings.title: Owner quotas drift when links are removed or imported
findings.description: Delete, Prune, Resolve, and the janitor can remove links without decrementing the owner's count. ImportAll adds links without updating counts. The quota dashboard can continue counting owners whose last link was removed and omit owners whose links were imported.

findings.title: Top returns the least followed links
findings.description: The list is sorted in ascending hit order before taking the first n entries, which reverses the documented ranking.

findings.title: Owner lookup matches substrings
findings.description: A lookup for ann also returns links owned by joann, and an empty owner string matches every link.

findings.title: Extending a link can shorten its lifetime or revive it
findings.description: Extend resets expiry to the current time plus ttl. This can shorten a live link's remaining lifetime and makes an expired link live again if the janitor has yet to remove it.

findings.title: The quota snapshot exposes mutable store state
findings.description: Quotas returns the backing dictionary. Clearing or editing the returned value changes the store's owner counts despite the method's snapshot contract.

findings.title: A failed batch import leaves earlier changes applied
findings.description: ImportAll validates each link immediately before inserting it. If a later entry has an invalid code, earlier entries remain inserted or overwritten even though the batch throws.

findings.title: Prune returns the number of surviving links
findings.description: Prune tracks how many entries it removes but returns the final dictionary count. Removing two of five links reports three removals.

findings.title: The dashboard error counter always reports zero
findings.description: No code increments errors, so the stats endpoint reports zero even after the service has returned a 500.

findings.title: Target checks classify URLs by scheme without checking reachability
findings.description: ProbeAsync waits briefly and returns whether the string starts with https://. CheckTargets therefore reports reachable HTTP targets as failures and passes HTTPS targets even when their hosts cannot be reached.

findings.title: Counting links for an unknown owner throws
findings.description: CountForOwner indexes the quota dictionary directly, so a fresh store or an owner with no entry produces a KeyNotFoundException instead of a count of zero.

findings.title: Faulted request tasks leave the HTTP response open
findings.description: The accept loop discards each handler task. A request without an Authorization header reaches BearerToken with an empty string and throws before Respond runs. The exception stays in the discarded task and the handler leaves the response open, so the client can wait until its own timeout.

findings.title: Deleting a link during a janitor tick can terminate the process
findings.description: The janitor gets a key from the live store dictionary and then looks it up separately. If Store.Delete removes that key between those steps, the indexer throws KeyNotFoundException. The exception escapes the timer callback and can terminate the process.

findings.title: Store readers enumerate dictionaries while other callers mutate them
findings.description: If TotalHits starts enumerating and ImportAll or Create inserts a new key before the next MoveNext, the enumeration throws InvalidOperationException. Page also copies the live values collection, and Followed returns a deferred query that enumerates it after the method returns.

findings.title: Parallel creates can lose an owner's quota increment
findings.description: For an owner with an existing quota entry, two Create calls can both read the same count and both write that count plus one. Both links can be inserted while the quota increases by only one. Quotas also exposes the live dictionary, allowing callers to change counts outside the store's control.

findings.title: Parallel code generation can overwrite a link
findings.description: Concurrent Create calls use the same Random instance without synchronization. Both can compute a code from the same generator state, and the unconditional assignment at line 40 lets the later write replace the first link.

findings.title: Parallel resolutions lose per-link hits
findings.description: Two Resolve calls that reach the hit increment for the same link can both read the same Hits value and write the same incremented value. Both return the target while the link records only one hit.

findings.title: Concurrent renames to the same code can discard a link
findings.description: Two callers renaming different links to the same free destination can both pass ContainsKey. Each then removes its source, and the last assignment to the destination overwrites the other link. Both callers can return successfully.

findings.title: Readers can observe a partially imported batch
findings.description: ImportAll publishes each link as it goes. A reader scheduled between two insertions can resolve or list the first imported link while the rest of the batch is still absent, violating the method's atomicity guarantee even when the batch is valid.

findings.title: Statistics can divide by zero when a concurrent operation removes the final link
findings.description: A stats call can finish TotalHits while a link is present, then read Count after a deletion or janitor tick removes that link. The division throws. Store.SuccessRate has the same race between its initial nonzero check and its final division.

findings.title: Session verification races with session issuance
findings.description: If Issue inserts a new token after Verify starts enumerating sessions, the next enumerator step can throw InvalidOperationException. Parallel Issue calls also share an unsynchronized Random, so they can generate the same token and replace one owner's session with another's.

findings.title: Cache inspection bypasses the lock used by writers
findings.description: Peek traverses the dictionary while Delete or Set can change its bucket chains. For example, if Peek has reached a colliding entry and Delete removes it before Peek follows the next entry, Peek can miss a key that stayed cached throughout the lookup. Utilization also reads the dictionary outside the lock, and Stats can read a torn hit count on a 32-bit runtime.

findings.title: Cache warming can replace a value inserted by another caller
findings.description: Warm can observe a missing key, then pause while another caller caches a fresh target for that key. Warm subsequently overwrites it with the older target from its input, even if Peek itself is made thread-safe.

findings.title: Concurrent metric updates lose creation counts
findings.description: Two AddCreated calls can read the same old value and both write that value plus one. Snapshot then undercounts successful creations. Its plain long reads can also tear on a 32-bit runtime.

findings.title: Stopping the janitor can leave a sweep running
findings.description: If a timer callback has already started, StopJanitor can return while the callback continues removing links or sweeping the cache. A second StartJanitor also replaces the only timer reference without disposing the previous timer, so callbacks from both timers can run.

findings.title: Cache warming returns before the scheduled writes finish
findings.description: WarmCache discards the task for every entry. A caller can immediately query the cache after WarmCache returns and miss a key whose write is still queued. Exceptions from the queued writes also stay in the discarded tasks.

findings.title: Target checks can deadlock on a single-threaded synchronization context
findings.description: If CheckTargets is called on a single-threaded synchronization context and ProbeAsync reaches an incomplete delay, the continuation is posted back to that context. The caller blocks the same thread on Result, so the continuation cannot run.

findings.title: Concurrent snapshot writes share one temporary file
findings.description: Writer A can finish writing the temporary file, then writer B can replace its contents before A moves it. A publishes B's payload to A's destination, and B's subsequent move fails because the temporary file is gone. The race also affects callers writing to different destination directories.

findings.title: Requests for the same report name can return each other's CSV
findings.description: Request A closes its export file before reopening it for the response. A concurrent request B using the same name can publish a different store snapshot in that interval. A then reads and returns B's report.

findings.title: Asynchronous exports expose neither completion nor write failures
findings.description: ExportCsvAsync returns void, so a background caller can proceed to read the report while the write is still pending. If the write fails, such as when the destination directory is missing, the exception escapes normal task observation and can terminate the process.

findings.title: Concurrent audit appends can reject one of the records
findings.description: Two callers can open the same audit path for append at the same time. On Windows, the first append's file share mode excludes another writer, so the second append can throw IOException and its audit record is left unwritten.

findings.title: Unauthenticated requests can exhaust listener connections
findings.description: A request with no Authorization header, or a header containing only one word, reaches an out-of-range array access before authentication. The exception faults the request task in Program.cs without sending a response or closing the connection. A remote client can repeat these requests across many connections and keep them outstanding, consuming listener resources and preventing legitimate clients from connecting.
